clue.text: Doubt maiden's yielding

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Someone questions whether a young woman is really submitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A misgiving is a feeling of uncertainty or apprehension, a close synonym for a doubt held about something.

clue.text: Mother's holding meeting — a source of eruptions

indicators.note: 'Mother has holding' means the word for mother wraps round the next piece

explanation.surface: A mother hosting a gathering that turns explosive.
explanation.walkthrough: AGM, for annual general meeting, is a common crossword abbreviation; the possessive 's here means 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Magma is molten rock beneath the earth's crust, which volcanoes throw out when they erupt.

clue.text: Eg, Liverpool game grips Everton and Anfield primarily

indicators.note: something that grips holds other material firmly inside itself
primarily points to the opening letter of each of the two club names

explanation.surface: Football in Liverpool, with Everton and Anfield taking centre stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Everton is a Liverpool football club and Anfield the ground of its rival; S(EA)PORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverpool is a major English port city on the Mersey, so it is an example of a harbour town.

clue.text: Reckless drive around Oxford University

indicators.note: around means the first piece is placed on either side of the second

parts.note: drive as in momentum or impulse

explanation.surface: A dangerous driver hurtling around the Oxford colleges.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetuous behaviour is rash and acts without thinking, which is what reckless conduct is.

clue.text: Show by example type of coffee I consumed

explanation.surface: A demonstration of what kind of coffee someone drank.
explanation.definitionFit: To instantiate is to represent an abstract idea through a concrete case or instance of it.

clue.text: Fuel cut — not keeping hot

indicators.note: not keeping means the word throws away one of its letters

parts.note: a gash is a deep cut
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A fuel reduction that leaves the heating off.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas, natural or bottled, is burned to produce heat, so it is a common kind of combustible energy source.

clue.text: Problem with a century plant

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A trouble with a hundred-year-old plant, perhaps in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumac is a shrub or small tree whose dried berries are also used as a spice.

clue.text: Clever Chinese dog, not English one

indicators.note: not tells us to drop from the breed name what follows

parts.note: the shar pei is a wrinkly Chinese breed
E is the abbreviation for English
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An intelligent Chinese dog that is not an English breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp person is quick-witted and astute, so the word is a synonym for bright or intelligent.

clue.text: Sentimental girl invited to see garden left home

parts.note: Tennyson's poem begins 'Come into the garden, Maud'
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A soppy tale of a girl asked to view a garden before leaving home.
explanation.walkthrough: The girl is Maud from Tennyson's poem 'Maud', whose famous line invites her into the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Maudlin means tearfully or self-pityingly emotional, an excessive form of being sentimental.

clue.text: Deposed dictator accuses EU for being thrown out

indicators.note: something thrown out is scattered, so the letters land in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An overthrown tyrant blaming the European Union for his expulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicolae Ceausescu was the Romanian communist leader overthrown and executed in 1989.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceausescu ruled Romania autocratically until a revolution toppled him, making him a classic ousted despot.

clue.text: Dolphin's mostly well out around slipway perhaps

indicators.note: around means the shortened phrase surrounds the next item
mostly means most of the phrase, so its final letter goes

parts.note: to well out is to gush
a slipway is a kind of ramp into the water

explanation.surface: A dolphin surging out of the sea near a boat slipway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' looks like a noun or adverb but is a verb here, meaning to pour out.
explanation.definitionFit: The grampus, also called Risso's dolphin, is a blunt-headed grey cetacean of the dolphin family.

clue.text: What might mix up a salt?

definitions.text: What might mix up a salt?

indicators.note: to mix things is to stir them into a new order

explanation.surface: A riddle about the kitchen tool used for stirring seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the letters of 'up a salt' rearranged give the tool that might do the mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: A spatula is a flat-bladed kitchen implement used to stir, blend and spread ingredients.

clue.text: Note fight in the vicinity

explanation.surface: A record of some local scuffle nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: About can mean nearby or around, as in 'there was nobody about', describing presence close at hand.

clue.text: A harvest and place to store it back in citadel

indicators.note: back tells us the storage word is to be read from its end

explanation.surface: A grain harvest and its storage barn tucked inside a fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: An acropolis is the fortified high part of an ancient Greek city, a stronghold such as the one in Athens.

clue.text: Umpire to falsify extended time given new time in cooler

parts.note: to rig results is to fake them
an era is a long period
N is the abbreviation for new
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A corrupt referee adding extra time, then landing in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' is slang for prison, which suits the surface; here it means something that cools.
explanation.definitionFit: A refrigerant is a substance used in fridges and air conditioners to absorb heat and lower temperature.

clue.text: Humour with appeal

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with; the answer also happening to sit inside this word is a coincidence

explanation.surface: Comedy that has charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Wit is clever verbal humour, the ability to say amusing things quickly and inventively.

clue.text: Oppose HST after understanding land's cut by line

indicators.note: cut by means losing what comes next from the word
after places the given trio of letters following the next item

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Resisting a high-speed train, with land sliced through by a railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: HST is a High Speed Train, a British intercity service; LAND loses its L to leave AND.
explanation.definitionFit: To withstand something is to resist it or hold out against it, so it means to stand in opposition.

clue.text: Like exhausted kangaroos that mustn't be touched

definitions.meaning: kangaroos that have run out of leaps, read literally
the idiom for something forbidden or off limits

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a playful cryptic reading of the phrase: a tired kangaroo has used up all its jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase normally describes a place or topic that is forbidden, while literally it can mean having no leaps left.

clue.text: Moved flag right onto higher part of church

indicators.note: letters that are moved shift into a different order

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A banner shifted to the right, up into the church's upper level.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ loft is the raised gallery in a church where the organ and often the choir are placed.

clue.text: Newspaper going all out for joint ownership scheme

parts.note: The Times, the paper this puzzle appears in
haring is running flat out like a hare

explanation.surface: A newspaper going hell for leather to promote a shared-property plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Timesharing is an arrangement where several people own a holiday property and each uses it for set weeks.

clue.text: Making fast million over old craze

definitions.note: a gerund standing for a noun: the act of tying up

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
O is the abbreviation for old
a rage is a fashion or fad

explanation.surface: Getting rich quick from a million on an old fad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like speed but here means secure, as in holding fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Moorage is the act of mooring a boat, that is, securing it in place with ropes or an anchor.

clue.text: Illness reportedly went quickly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard spoken, so we go by the pronunciation

parts.note: flew is the past tense of fly, to go fast

explanation.surface: An illness that is said to have passed swiftly.
explanation.definitionFit: Flu, short for influenza, is a common viral infection causing fever and aches.

clue.text: Fine good-for-nothing over blade

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means flipped so it reads upwards

parts.note: a waster is an idle wastrel

explanation.surface: A decent but idle person messing about with a knife.
explanation.definitionFit: A fretsaw is a fine-bladed saw used for cutting intricate curves in wood, so it is a cutting blade.

clue.text: Fine example of hospice we renovated

indicators.note: something renovated is rebuilt, so its letters are restructured

explanation.surface: The care home we refurbished is a model building.
explanation.definitionFit: A showpiece is an outstanding item displayed as a model of its kind, a fine specimen.

clue.text: Very old king I spotted in carriage

indicators.note: in places the single letter inside the vehicle word

explanation.surface: An elderly monarch seen riding in a coach.
explanation.definitionFit: Priam was the aged king of Troy in Greek legend, so he is literally a king from ancient times.

clue.text: Poor in seven days if losing regularly

indicators.note: losing regularly means every other letter is thrown away

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Someone who will be broke within a week if they keep losing.
explanation.definitionFit: Needy describes people lacking money or necessities, which is what being poor means.

clue.text: Sing unknown poem by learner

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: Performing an obscure verse written by a novice.
explanation.definitionFit: To yodel is to sing with rapid switches between chest voice and falsetto, as in Alpine folk song.

clue.text: Very impressive river, one where nothing is good

indicators.note: where nothing is means one letter takes the place of the zero shape

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A spectacular river where nothing at all is any good.
explanation.walkthrough: The second O of AMAZON is replaced by I, then G follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazing means causing great wonder or astonishment, a strong synonym for remarkable or impressive.

clue.text: Yak burgers, fat and cabbage hearts

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter

parts.note: the central letter of each of the three words; the run reversed inside cabbage is a coincidence

explanation.surface: A Himalayan ox eating burgers, fat and cabbage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yak' looks like the animal but is the verb meaning to chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: To gab is to talk at length idly, the same as to yak or chatter.

clue.text: Eudora's strangely excited

indicators.note: strangely means out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters as printed, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A woman called Eudora is oddly worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Aroused means stirred up or stimulated, so it serves as a synonym for excited.

clue.text: Ideal shot bags fifth of wickets

indicators.note: to bag something is to pocket it, so it goes inside

parts.note: a shot of whisky is a dram

indicators.note: fifth of picks out the letter in position five

explanation.surface: A perfect delivery that takes wickets in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream as a noun or adjective can mean something perfect, as in a dream house or the ideal.

clue.text: City to west end of the lake is drier

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for west

indicators.note: end of means we keep only the final letter of the following word

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A city west of a lake is less damp than elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drier' reads as a comparative adjective but is a noun: something that dries you.
explanation.definitionFit: A bath towel is a large towel used for drying oneself after bathing, so it is a thing that dries.
